data.title: Making planks for the Bojná hillfort – a historical carpentry course
data.excerpt: Over the weekend of 3–4 October 2020 several members of our association took part in a course in historical carpentry techniques organised by the village of Bojná. Under the expert guidance of Ing. Július Lišaník we tried out how to turn a tree into dressed planks using only an axe, wedges and a handsaw – planks that can be used on the gate of the Bojná hillfort.
data.metaTitle: Making planks for the Bojná hillfort
data.metaDescription: Members of our association at a course in historical carpentry techniques in Bojná (2020) — planks made by hand from a tree with an axe and wedges (J. Lišaník).

children.text: Over the weekend of 3–4 October 2020 several members of our association took part in a very interesting course organised by the village of Bojná under the title Kurz historickej tesárskej techniky (A Course in Historical Carpentry Techniques). Under the expert guidance of Ing. Július Lišaník we thus tried out at first hand (and on our own muscles) how to make dressed planks out of a tree using only such tools as an axe, wedges or a handsaw, which were available to our Slavic ancestors. Besides us, several other volunteers took part in the course (for example the Falconers of King Svatopluk), and together we made a number of planks that can be used to repair, or rather to finish, the gate of the Bojná hillfort. For us laymen it was a demanding task, but after the effort the result came. We thank the mayor of Bojná for looking after us so well throughout the course, when we had an abundance of Slavic food and drink. At the end of the day on Sunday we also tried out another piece of experimental archaeology – shooting a period bow through the loopholes of the entrance gate and the crenellations in the palisades, which was also very interesting. Below you can look at a short photo report.
